title: 10 Big Cases of Revenge
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss revenge across history and pop culture. They open with revenge as a theme in movies and the Code of Hammurabi's eye-for-an-eye justice, then count down a "top ten" of revenge cases: the Spam King Alan Ralsky-style spammer's home address being leaked and trolled (named Alan Rowski in the transcript), the forty-seven ronin's revenge for their master's forced seppuku, the St. Bartholomew's Day massacre of Huguenots after a Paris wedding, Dr. Hawley Harvey Crippen's murder of his wife Cora, Lorena Bobbitt's cutting of John Wayne Bobbitt, Anthony Stockelman's prison tattoo "Katie's Revenge" after he murdered Katie Coleman, and the Dachau massacre by American soldiers in World War Two. They also cover revenge movie lists, a Tarantino/Alan Ball neighbor dispute, a listener-facing Kiva loan milestone, and a short cannibalism listener-mail-style reading from a New Mexico biology student. Listeners are invited to send revenge stories.

segments.title: Opening banter on revenge and Hammurabi
segments.summary: Hosts joke about their love of comeuppance and revenge in movies, then discuss the Code of Hammurabi and the eye-for-an-eye principle as the origin of codified revenge and the justice system.

segments.title: Revenge in primate and human brains
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss revenge as ancient and linked to the brain's pleasure centers, and how they personally enjoy seeing revenge played out in movies.

segments.title: Spam king's comeuppance
segments.summary: Alan Rowski, known as the Spam King, is discussed. After a local paper profiled his large house, trolls leaked his address and signed him up for junk mail. He was later jailed on a 2009 securities case involving a penny stock scheme.

segments.title: Forty-seven ronin
segments.summary: Explanation of ronin and samurai loyalty, then the story of Asano Naganori drawing his sword in Kyoto, his seppuku, and the forty-seven ronin who waited two years to take revenge on Kira Yoshinaka before turning themselves in and committing seppuku.

segments.title: St. Bartholomew's Day massacre
segments.summary: The 1572 Paris wedding between a Huguenot aristocrat and a Catholic is described, followed by King Charles IX ordering the killing of Huguenot leaders and a week-long massacre of thousands of Protestants in Paris and the countryside.

segments.title: Hawley Harvey Crippen
segments.summary: Crippen, a homeopathic doctor in London, allegedly killed his singer wife Cora after she learned of his mistress and left him. He was convicted and hanged; later forensic evidence in 2007 suggested the body was not his wife's.

segments.title: Lorena Bobbitt
segments.summary: Lorena Bobbitt cut off part of her husband John Wayne Bobbitt's penis after years of alleged abuse. She was found not guilty by reason of temporary insanity, and the hosts discuss his later films and her founding of a women's abuse nonprofit.

segments.title: Anthony Stockelman and Katie's Revenge
segments.summary: Stockelman was sentenced to life for the molestation and murder of ten-year-old Katie Coleman. In prison, his cellmate Jared Harris, Katie's cousin, tattooed 'Katie's Revenge' on his forehead; Stockelman was later assaulted and the tattoo was done under threat.

segments.title: Dachau massacre
segments.summary: After the American Thunderbird Division liberated Dachau and found the death train, soldiers killed unarmed SS officers and German guards; a classified army investigation was filed and buried until the Boston Globe series in the 2000s brought it to light.

segments.title: Tarantino and Alan Ball neighbor dispute
segments.summary: Brief digression on Quentin Tarantino's lawsuit against neighbor Alan Ball over noisy pet birds in an aviary.

segments.title: Revenge movies lists
segments.summary: The hosts discuss revenge movie lists from Film School Rejects and others, including Commando, Gladiator, Kill Bill, Death Wish, Old Boy, Carrie, The Virgin Spring, I Spit on Your Grave, and Taken.

segments.title: Kiva loan milestone
segments.summary: The hosts celebrate the podcast's Kiva lending team reaching one million dollars in loans and plan for a new goal.

segments.title: Cannibalism listener reading
segments.summary: Chuck reads a listener email from a University of New Mexico biology student about disease transmission and the origins of cannibalism in humans and chimps, and the hosts point to their older cannibalism episode.

segments.title: Sign-off and listener call for revenge stories
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to send their own non-internet revenge stories via Twitter, Facebook, or email and promote a video podcast.
